status: shipped: registered in STRIP_UNITS and exported with strips.py export (#1627, #759)
generator: ChatGPT image generation (project owner, paid plan)
prompts: Based on scripts/sprite-puppet/strip-rigs/swordsman.json. The master came from a create-from-scratch prompt (a medieval swordsman: riveted helmet with nose guard, chainmail, red tabard, large round steel shield from chin to hip, arming sword held up clear of the shield, two separate legs, flat magenta background, red only on the tabard). The damage sheet, attack strip, hit strip and defeat strip were each drawn in a separate message from the master as one 'Draw ONE image: the ... sheet' prompt per image, all on flat magenta, with the master attached each time. The prompt text used is the one in the strip prompt set written for this unit (the plan kept under .verification/strips/swordsman/chatgpt-prompts-v2.md in the working tree, not committed). Red appears only on the tabard so the team tint lands only there; stains and scratches are dark grey, brown, dark maroon or black. The sword stays in his hand and the shield on his arm in every frame, including the defeat strip. The prompts ChatGPT actually ran were not captured verbatim.
licence_note: Covered by the project's non-commercial posture (docs/asset-rights-ledger.md). This art ships in the game; it is counted in the ledger family 'ChatGPT image generation (unit strips)' and this record is its provenance.
originals_note: The downloaded originals are not committed (kept under ~/conquestoria-art-originals/strips/swordsman). Only the re-encoded sheet.png and mask.png are, built by scripts/sprite-puppet/strips.py from decoded pixels (no EXIF/XMP/ICC or C2PA survives).
scan: python3 -I scripts/portrait-pixelate/portrait_pixelate.py scan: all five passed (PNG magic bytes, nothing after the image stream, clean decode, one frame). ClamAV was not installed, so only the structural checks ran.
regenerations: Several drafts were rejected before these were accepted. (1) The first master drew a small buckler instead of a shield and its defeat frames would have put the sword on the ground (sha256 9b27c8aa391b3d4f03235cc86ceec0049ab9fd4640c6f20f418e13d618e7c5b7, kept as swordsman_try/a.png in the originals folder). (2) A second master with a large shield had the sword blade crossing the shield; it was redrawn with the blade held clear of the shield and that redraw is the accepted master (the rejected one was not downloaded). (3) The first damage prompt, written as a long multi-image preamble, came back as a checklist with no image; it was rewritten as a short single-image prompt and the damage sheet was drawn on the next try. (4) The first hit-reaction request drew a second attack strip instead (kept in the originals folder as d-v1-wrong-image-attack-again.png, sha256 94d4a9bc21f72d377c418b93466cf33463847566d1843ad2015f5fcf5bdcc659); the accepted hit sheet came from a new conversation whose prompt began by saying it was a different image from any earlier one. Known caveat: the probe warns that the prone figure on the defeat sheet is 183 px tall (under 300), accepted because that is the pose, not a zoom.
